title: Nature hunt
offscreen: Bring home just one treasure, already fallen on the ground, and put it on a little plate: it's the start of your nature table.

items.label: A fallen leaf
items.say: Look for a leaf that has fallen on the ground. The ones on the trees stay there.

items.label: A smooth stone
items.say: Now a smooth stone, as small as your hand.

items.label: A fallen twig
items.say: And a fallen twig. How does it feel?

items.label: A seed or an acorn
items.say: Look for a seed, an acorn or a pine cone.

items.label: A fallen petal
items.say: Now a petal that has fallen on the ground. We don't pull flowers off.

items.label: A little creature to look at
items.say: Look for a little creature, an ant or a ladybird. We don't pick it up: look at it and come and tell me what it's like.

items.label: A piece of bark
items.say: And a little piece of fallen bark. Smell it: what does it smell of?

intro.bo: {nome}, shall we go on a treasure hunt? You look in your own time, one thing at a time.
intro.pilu: {nome}, I'll tell you something to look for. Look carefully around you: treasures are everywhere.
intro.tango: Treasure hunt, {nome}! I'm coming too! ...No, I'll stay here. You look, slowly.

outro.bo: So many treasures, {nome}. Now each one goes back in its place, so we can find them again tomorrow.
outro.pilu: Every treasure goes back where you found it, {nome}: that's part of the game too.
outro.tango: What a hunt! {nome}, shall we put everything back? I'll... I'll keep an eye on it.
